prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1325; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound on a two-lane road in Conroe, Texas, when the vehicle ahead of Driver 2 slowed and Driver 2 was unable to stop in time. The two vehicles made contact in a low-speed head-on collision. Both drivers were able to exit their vehicles under their own power, and the Passenger seated in the front right position was also present at the scene. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated on scene before being transported for further care. Witnesses, scene photographs, and Driver 2's statement all agree with the sequence of events as Driver 1 described it. The front-end damage on both vehicles is consistent with the reported impact and the speeds involved. Officers noted a few old scratches on the lower bumper of Driver 1's vehicle, which may predate this collision and were documented separately. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers confirmed through witness accounts and scene observation that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of impact.
